title: Authorization cartridge for customer-managed networking: PRD draft
content:
Purpose / brief

This doc sketches a lightweight, pluggable ‘authorization cartridge’ that sits alongside Private deployments (customer-managed networking / VPCs) to standardize approval gates and compact audit capture. The cartridge should make operator workflows auditable, fast for routine changes, and provable for compliance reviews without shipping full heavy-weight attestation bundles for every change.

Problem statement
- Customers building on Private want: low-friction network changes (DNS, route updates, firewall rules) while retaining an auditable chain of custody for regulatory/compliance use cases.
- Current options: full evidence bundles (heavy, slow) or opaque logs with poor indexability. Both create friction or risk.
- Need: a developer-friendly, operator-friendly module that provides: incremental attestation stamps, a compact audit index, and approval fastlane patterns.

Goals (measurable)
1) Reduce median time-to-approve for routine operator changes from manual-review ~20m to ~2m for low-risk changes under canned policies.
2) Produce compact, queryable audit events (<= 2KB per-change) that satisfy SOC-like evidence requests for routine changes.
3) Provide pluggable operator SDK so customers can adapt to internal RBAC and HSM/KMS integration.
4) Default to privacy-preserving payloads — minimize PII/sensitive data in the audit index while allowing for full evidence download under strict controls.

Non-goals
- This is not a full replacement for cryptographic notarization or escrowed evidence for high-risk changes (that remains as an advanced option).
- Not building a custom KMS — we integrate with customer KMS/HSM or Redwood KMS only for prototype.

Scope (what’s in / out)
In scope:
- Approval fastlane for routine network changes (route add/removal, security-group tweaks, DNS TTL updates) with canned policy templates.
- Compact audit record format and index service able to store, search, and export events.
- Local operator UI widgets (Console) and CLI hooks for Private deployments.
- Integrations: customer KMS (optional), SIEM forwarder (syslog/CEF), optional signed receipts.
Out of scope:
- Deep forensic snapshot replays (advanced forensic tooling exists elsewhere).
- Changes to core network dataplane implementation — cartridge reads the change metadata and speaks to control plane APIs.

Design overview
- Cartridge = small microservice + SDK + Console/CLI components.
- Responsibilities: present approval prompt (via Console/CLI), evaluate policy, collect minimal change evidence, emit compact audit event, and optionally request a signed receipt from a signing provider (customer HSM or Redwood).
- Policy engine: hierarchical policies (tenant -> operator role -> route-type) with simple risk scoring. Low-risk auto-approve via fastlane. Medium/high require explicit human approval and produce richer evidence bundles.

Compact audit record (proposal)
- single-line JSON (kept minimal) stored in indexer and forwarded to SIEM:
  - id: uuid-v4
  - ts: ISO8601
  - actor_id: operator-id (opaque hash)
  - action: enum (route_add, security_group_update, dns_change)
  - target: short descriptor (e.g., subnet:10.2.0.0/24)
  - policy_decision: allow|deny|escalate
  - risk_score: 0-100
  - evidence_ref: short pointer to encrypted evidence blob (only for escalations or on-demand)
  - signature: optional compact signature token (base64)
Notes: keep payload < 2KB and avoid embedding full configs. Evidence blobs are stored encrypted and accessible via a narrow ACL.

Approval fastlane UX patterns
- Canned low-risk change: operator invokes CLI/Console -> pre-check returns risk_score <= threshold -> cartridge emits audit event with auto-approve flag and returns immediate control-plane token to apply change.
- Human in the loop: pre-check returns risk_score > threshold -> notification to approvers (Slack/email/Console) with compact summary + approve/deny links -> upon approval, cartridge attaches signed receipt and releases change token.
- Delegated operator tokens: time-limited tokens for trusted operators (expires TTL, tied to KMS key). Useful for devops teams that need repeated low-risk changes.

Evidence lifecycle and retention
- Compact audit index: hot store (90 days) optimized for querying and SIEM forwards.
- Evidence blobs: encrypted and stored in cold storage with retention policy configured per-customer (default 1 year). Blobs unlocked only for authorized roles or during audits.
- Redaction: cartridge may automatically redact IP/payloads from the compact event and keep full details only in the evidence blob.

Security & compliance considerations
- Customer-managed keys: prefer HSM-backed signing; Redwood supports optional integration to fetch compact receipts signed with customer key.
- Tamper-evidence: include hash chain on compact events (rolling anchor) optional to provide simple tamper detection for customers who want it.
- Minimal privilege: cartridge service runs with least privilege to read control-plane metadata; never stores customer secrets in plaintext.

Observability & ops
- Console: per-tenant timeline view, quick filter by change type, risk-score histogram.
- Traces: distributed traces for approval latency and carving per-change SLOs.
- Alerts: devops alert if auto-approve rate deviates >10% week-over-week (possible policy drift).

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (lab): internal prototype with Redwood KMS, run against internal Private testbeds. (4 weeks)
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 2 strategic customers, support customer KMS, SIEM forwarder, gather feedback. (8–12 weeks)
- Phase 2 (general availability): hardened UI, RBAC hooks, retention controls, docs & runbook. (6 weeks after pilot signoff)

Open questions / risks
- How do we price evidence storage and SIEM forwarding for customers who generate high volumes of low-risk changes? (ops cost risk)
- Is our risk scoring sufficiently defensible for auditors? Need to define risk model and allowed inputs.
- HSM integration complexity across cloud vendors — prototype minimal feature first (signed receipts optional).

Next steps / immediate TODOs
- Product: draft policy templates for common infra patterns (dns-ttl-bump, internal-subnet-route-add) — owner: Priya — due: 2025-11-16.
- Eng (APIs): define compact event schema and index API contract — owner: Marco — due: 2025-11-30.
- Security: threat model for cartridge and KMS integration — owner: Ethan — due: 2025-12-07.
- Schedule pilot customers and create pilot checklist (data retention SLA, KMS onboarding).

Notes to self / sketchy ideas
- Consider a ‘change cartridge marketplace’ later where customers can drop custom validators (small WASM modules) to run domain-specific checks before approval.
- Could offer a cheap immutable anchor option (daily batch anchoring hash to an append-only ledger) as an anti-tamper add-on.

Attachments / references
- linked tickets (see linked_artifacts above)
- short mockups: console snapshots to be attached in Confluence page (WIP)

Feedback requested from reviewers
- Is the compact event model sufficient for standard SIEM ingestion? What fields are missing?
- Any legal/compliance stakeholders we should loop in early (auditability requirements can vary by region).

-- end of sketch --

(Internal draft — expect lots of change; keep informal notes here. Will migrate finalized schema to the API spec once we lock the contract.)
